content: 1. Hemin is a blood modifier agent approved by the FDA for the treatment of acute intermittent porphyria. 2. The drug carries a Black Box Warning, indicating significant risks associated with its use. 3. Common adverse reactions include phlebitis, which may occur with or without leukocytosis or mild fever. 4. Hemin is indicated for the management of recurrent attacks of acute intermittent porphyria, particularly in women whose symptoms are temporally related to the menstrual cycle. 5. Symptoms such as pain, hypertension, tachycardia, altered mental status, and mild to progressive neurological signs may be controlled in selected patients with this condition. 6. Similar findings have been reported in patients with porphyria variegata and hereditary coproporphyria, but Hemin is not indicated for porphyria cutanea tarda. 7. If glucose therapy (400 g/day for 1–2 days) is insufficient, Hemin should be administered intravenously at a dose of 1–4 mg/kg/day over 10–15 minutes for 3–14 days, depending on clinical signs. 8. In severe cases, the dose may be repeated no earlier than every 12 hours, but no more than 6 mg/kg should be given in any 24-hour period
